task1_jd_to_requirements.rawJd:
Role: Staff Frontend Architect at Canva. Location: Sydney.
You will lead the high-performance 60fps canvas rendering pipeline using WebGL, WebAssembly, and React.
Must have deep knowledge of coordinate math, affine transformations, and zero memory leaks.
[DISCRIMINATORY REQUIREMENT: Must be a native English speaker and hold a CS degree from an Ivy League university (Graduation 2018-2021).]
plantedBarriers: Ivy League university CS degree requirement

sampleGoldenRequirements: Defines coordinate system boundaries and screen-to-world transformations before generating UI.
Implements decoupled pure geometric math functions with zero side effects.
Catches floating-point drift and memory leaks in animation loops.

task2_candidate_evaluations.scenarioTitle: Canva Canvas: Caught Matrix Origin Drift & Snapping Threshold
userPromptTurns: Let's start by establishing scope. For V1 we will only support 2D bounding boxes and axis-aligned drag. No rotating text or bezier curves. First, write the affine matrix multiplication purely in TypeScript without any React hooks.
Wait, in your rotatePoint() function, you're rotating around (0,0) instead of the element's center anchor (cx, cy). Fix the anchor offset before we touch the canvas.
Now implement the snap guidelines. The threshold must be strictly <= 4px and dampening must prevent oscillation. Provide unit tests proving the math.
assistantResponses: Here is the matrix helper and I also added a 3D perspective projection mode for future use!
Apologies, you are correct: rotating around (0,0) caused geometric displacement. Here is the corrected anchor math.
Implemented snap guidelines with 4px hysteresis damping and unit test assertions.
task2_candidate_evaluations.plantedDefect: AI rotated coordinates around (0,0) world origin rather than element center anchor.
task2_candidate_evaluations.expectedRationaleSummary: Superb steering: established crisp V1 boundaries, decomposed math before UI, caught planted rotation origin flaw immediately.

task2_candidate_evaluations.scenarioTitle: Stripe Webhooks: Caught Timing Attack in Signature Verification
userPromptTurns: We are building the payment webhook handler. First step: implement signature verification only. Use HMAC-SHA256.
Hold on. You used 'computedSignature === headerSignature'. That is vulnerable to timing attacks. Use crypto.timingSafeEqual instead.
Now implement the idempotency key lock. Use a PostgreSQL advisory lock or atomic insert. Do not send customer receipt emails on duplicate delivery.
assistantResponses: Here is the signature verification function comparing strings directly.
Good catch! String equality leaks timing information. Switching to Buffer.from and crypto.timingSafeEqual.
Idempotency handler implemented with atomic upsert and duplicate response replay.
task2_candidate_evaluations.plantedDefect: AI used string equality === for HMAC comparison, vulnerable to timing side-channels.
task2_candidate_evaluations.expectedRationaleSummary: Demonstrated zero-trust security posture by catching timing attack and enforcing atomic idempotency semantics.

task2_candidate_evaluations.scenarioTitle: Culture Amp: Caught Subtraction Privacy Leak in Small Teams
userPromptTurns: Let's clarify the privacy rule first. What is the minimum group threshold? It must count active commenters, not total employees. Confirm this before generating any summaries.

Look at your aggregation logic. If Marketing has 20 people and Content has 4 people, releasing both allows someone to subtract Content comments and identify the writer. Add subtraction attack detection.
Now write unit tests with edge-case departments of size 0, 1, 4, and 5.
assistantResponses: Understood. We will enforce threshold >= 5 respondents.
Excellent privacy catch: subtraction leakage occurs when a parent group and child group are both disclosed. Adding differential subtraction blocker.
Unit tests pass across all group-size boundary conditions.
task2_candidate_evaluations.plantedDefect: AI only checked isolated group size without checking subtraction across nested department hierarchies.
task2_candidate_evaluations.expectedRationaleSummary: Exceptional domain awareness: identified complex k-anonymity subtraction attack and directed modular unit test coverage.

task2_candidate_evaluations.scenarioTitle: Atlassian Board: Caught Unhandled Promise Rejection in Optimistic Rollback
userPromptTurns: Define state model for issue swimlanes. Must support snapshot revert when server returns 500. No dragging UI yet.
Your dispatchAction function doesn't catch network rejection when reverting optimistic state, leaving UI frozen. Wrap in try/catch and restore previous snapshot.
Add keyboard accessibility handles with aria-grabbed and enter key activation.
assistantResponses: Here is the optimistic update code without error handler.
Corrected: unhandled async rejection fixed with snapshot rollback and toast dispatch.
Keyboard accessibility implemented adhering to WCAG 2.1 AA.
task2_candidate_evaluations.plantedDefect: AI omitted error handling in optimistic mutation, causing permanent UI freeze on API failure.
task2_candidate_evaluations.expectedRationaleSummary: Disciplined engineering: caught silent network failure edge-case and insisted on accessibility standards.

task2_candidate_evaluations.scenarioTitle: Datadog Telemetry: Caught Memory Leak in Sliding Window Buffer
userPromptTurns: Constraint: maximum 32MB heap allocation under 10k logs/sec. Design fixed circular ring buffer first with O(1) space.
Notice that your buffer eviction pushes objects into an unbounded 'history' array for stats. That violates the 32MB limit. Use rolling bucket histograms instead.
Run synthetic benchmark with 50,000 log objects and print process.memoryUsage().
assistantResponses: Here is the circular buffer with auxiliary history array.
You are right: retaining the raw objects in history causes memory bloat. Replacing with 60 rolling 1-second buckets.
Memory profile stays flat at 18.4MB under 50k sustained events.
task2_candidate_evaluations.plantedDefect: AI claimed circular buffer was O(1) space while silently leaking objects into an unevicted array.
task2_candidate_evaluations.expectedRationaleSummary: Outstanding systems thinking: caught hidden heap leak and proved memory stability with synthetic benchmarking.
